morning.title: B-1B Bombers Make Hasty Departure From England
morning.text:
U.S. Air Force B-1B Lancer bombers that had been deployed to RAF Fairford in the U.K. since operation Epic Fury have returned to their home stations, a U.S. defense official confirmed to TWZ. The hasty movement was reportedly sparked by new Iranian threats against the base, although the Pentagon doesn’t confirm that assertion.

The sudden withdrawal came a week after a major incident was declared near Fairford following the arrest of five men on suspicion of driving bomb-laden vans toward it. They were later released on bail after no explosives were found. However, Counter-Terrorism police are continuing the investigation and said they were considering ​whether a foreign ​state had ⁠been involved. On Wednesday, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the incident might have had an Iranian ​link.

The Wall Street Journal was the first to report the departure.

Bomber strikes launched from Fairford, which included ones executed by both B-1s and B-52s, were a central aspect of major U.S. combat operations against Iran earlier this year. In addition, the installation is a major hub for U.S. military aircraft in the United Kingdom. It is a regular host of strategic assets, including bombers and U-2 spy planes. It also acts as a pit stop for other aircraft, including fighters, that are being ferried to and from the United States.

The U.S. withdrew all 12 B-1s “after commanders received new threats about an Iran-backed plot against the installation,” The New York Times reported, citing two U.S. officials.

“The withdrawal was highly unusual: Such moves are rarely made so quickly from an allied air base in a peacetime country thousands of miles from a combat zone,” the publication added. “The need to move the bombers out of the base, R.A.F. Fairford, was deemed so urgent that some of the planes and their flight crews left while aerial refueling aircraft were still being scrambled to support their flights to the United States. At least three of the planes had landed at their home base in South Dakota by Sunday.”

U.S. officials declined to tell the Times the specific nature of the new information that prompted the Lancer withdrawal, some of which had just arrived in the past week as part of a normal rotation of forces to maintain the B-1 forward presence in Europe.

“One U.S. official said the new information was part of the same threat warnings that surfaced three weeks ago, but specific details and a sense of urgency spiked in the past 24 hours, alarming commanders,” the publication noted.

As we previously reported, Tehran directly threatened RAF Fairford in July over its use as a base to launch attacks against Iran.

“The American aggressor army, which used to launch cruise missiles from its vessels in the Indian Ocean in its aggression after the official resumption of the war, with the end of the missile reserves of the aforementioned vessels, yesterday switched to using B1 planes flying from Fairford Air Base, England,” Tasnim News Agency, a quasi-state outlet in Iran with ties to the country’s powerful Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), claimed on Telegram on July 23. “As the officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs also stated, any base that is used to invade Iran’s territory is our legitimate goal.”

Local aircraft spotters and aviation photographers began to notice the aircraft departing in large numbers earlier on Sunday.

The aircraft left in several waves, according to the DefenceGeek X account, run by the senior editor of the U.K. Defence Journal.

The defense official who confirmed the withdrawal said the aircraft movements won’t affect overall readiness.

“The Airmen that operate America’s bomber force, including B-1s, B-2s, and B-52s, remain ready to deliver precision global strike capabilities – including through operations that launch and recover from the continental United States – anywhere, anytime,” the official added.

When we asked the Pentagon about the retrograde movement of bombers from the U.K., they did not confirm the security issue that prompted it, stating:

“U.S. Air Force bombers routinely operate around the world to support global force readiness and operational requirements. While operational security precluded us from confirming the movement of our assets and forces in real-time, we can acknowledge now that all U.S. bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have re-deployed to their home stations in the United States. The Airmen that operate America’s bomber force, including B-1s, B-2s, and B-52s, remain ready to deliver precision global strike capabilities – including through operations that launch and recover from the continental United States – anywhere, anytime.”

Regardless, this is the first time in months that RAF Fairford has not hosted U.S. bombers.

Contact the author: howard@twz.com

Blockbuster Accenture show holds out hope for battered Indian IT
morning.text: Mumbai: Accenture surged more than a fifth Thursday - a record for the global technology services leader and rare for a company with more than $100 billion in market value. It holds out hope for Indian IT - still the Nifty's third largest by weighting after financials and energy - and is a timely reminder to investors that they may have written the $315-billion industry's obituary rather prematurely.Yet, it would be equally premature to assume Accenture's standout FY26 performance and robust guidance for next year would trigger an immediate re-rating for India's listed outsourcing pureplay.134683373Investor enthusiasm for Infosys and Wipro American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), which climbed up to 8% on Oct 1, reflects scarcity premium rather than belief in an immediate sectoral turnaround, although some analysts believe the depressed valuations (table attached) adequately reflect the industry's AI-spawned revenue risks.Against this backdrop, Accenture's earnings at least helped re-establish the industry's commercial viability in the AI era.Read more: Will Nifty, Sensex plunge for 9th straight week? TCS Q2, RBI MPC among 4 factors to drive Dalal Street from MondayIts healthy book-to-bill ratio shows that tech services companies have regained the ability to translate promises (orders) into reality (sales). Those harnessing AI to make a strategic difference to their clients should see their addressable universe expand - not shrink. Accenture's last FY performance proved that even managed services engagements - or pure-play, cost-focused outsourcing, the mainstay of Indian IT - are becoming more value-loaded."Our managed services-led work also includes significant consulting and AI expertise, as many clients use this work to both reinvent and to get greater certainty around outcomes, including cost savings," Accenture CEO Julie Sweet told analysts in the conference call after the earnings. "Against this backdrop, two things stand out. First, our largest client relationships continue to expand as clients take on broader, more strategic transformations. The second standout is how our AI demand is broadening because of both the depth and breadth of our expertise."Read more: After Nifty’s longest losing streak in 25 years, what should investors do now?AI-Era ExpertiseThe key for Indian IT to extract a re-rating from analysts, following this year's 14% retreat in the Nifty IT index, is to help expand this 'depth and breadth of expertise' - something Accenture harnessed for 141 quarterly client bookings exceeding $100 million each. Separately, stable and improving margins close to 16% indicate moderation in pricing pressures, while a 6% revenue guidance - matching the highest in four years - suggests a modest revival in discretionary spending by clients."Accenture's results, commentary and guidance are slightly positive for Indian IT. Guidance of recovery in consulting business alludes to early signs of possible recovery in discretionary spends, though not in the immediate future," Nuvama said in a report. "We... maintain that Gen AI will eventually lead to expansion of TAM for Indian IT companies." Not long ago, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) trumped both Accenture and IBM in the market capitalization sweepstakes. So, re-establishing relevance in the AI era - with billions of dollars in idle cash on balance sheets - shouldn't be beyond the reach of top companies in a sector where India remains the unchallenged global leader.

morning.title: September IPO rush draws $1 billion FPI money even as listed stocks see record outflows
morning.text: ET Intelligence Group: The relentless flow of IPOs in September kept FPIs busy buying in the Indian primary market even as they accelerated selling in listed equities. They invested $1 billion (₹9,676 crore) in the primary market while offloading $4.8 billion (₹45,537 crore) worth of equities in the secondary market during the month, the highest since April 2026 when the outflow was $6.7 billion (₹63,167 crore).Of the 96 IPOs in 2026 so far, 34 were hosted in September alone. It implies that one out of every three IPOs this year so far was crammed in a single month as IPO-bound companies scrambled to dodge the requirement of filing audited financials for the current fiscal year's recent quarters.134683098Read more: Will Nifty, Sensex plunge for 9th straight week? TCS Q2, RBI MPC among 4 factors to drive Dalal Street from MondayIt also means the pace of primary market offerings may cool off in October since companies would take time to gather audited financial data for the June and subsequent quarters in the current fiscal year. Still, the expected launch of the Jio Platforms IPO in the second half of October may offer some support to the primary market investments given its anticipated size of over ₹35,000 crore-40,000 crore.Read more: After Nifty’s longest losing streak in 25 years, what should investors do now?FPIs have invested $5.9 billion in the primary market while selling $33.7 billion worth of equities in the secondary market in 2026 till the end of September. This compares with a net inflow of $5 billion in the primary market and an outflow of $22.7 billion from the secondary market in the corresponding period of the previous year. It means they continue to show interest in new equity papers while offloading their stakes in listed counters. Primary markets offer an opportunity to buy into businesses with strong growth potential, usually at a discount to the valuations of existing listed peers. Also, it does not involve the impact of bulk deals on stock prices as in the secondary market.

morning.title: Next-gen GST to boost growth, ease compliance
morning.text: India's ambition to become a Viksit Bharat requires an economy in which enterprises of every size can grow, wherever they begin. Over the past 12 years, our government has worked to create those conditions. GST's introduction in 2017 established a common national framework for indirect taxation. Next-gen GST carries that effort forward, drawing on nine years of implementation and the experience of taxpayers and states.Under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision, next-gen GST was conceived with two connected purposes: to reduce and rationalise rates, and to make compliance easier. The rate changes took effect on September 22, 2025. The next phase of process reforms will come before the GST Council shortly. Together, these efforts seek to give households relief, businesses greater certainty and taxpayers a system in which they can fulfil their obligations without avoidable difficulty.Also Read: GST 2.0 may scrap arrest powers, raise prosecution barStates have been partners throughout. They brought their priorities and experience to the council, helped shape the decisions and undertook their implementation. I thank them for that commitment.The results provide grounds for confidence. Between October 2025 and July 2026, the value of reported taxable supplies grew 25.8% over the corresponding period a year earlier. A lighter rate structure has been accompanied by a substantial expansion in reported economic activity. This is an encouraging foundation for a reform intended to support both enterprise and public finances.Also Read: India within reach of 8% growth, says Ex-RBI guvThat resilience is visible in the latest revenue figures. Gross GST collections reached ₹12.46 lakh crore during April-September 2026, up 11.6% from a year earlier. Every month from June through September recorded double-digit annual growth; together, collections for these four months accelerated by nearly 15%. Net collections, after refunds, grew 10.4% over the half-year. Taxpayer relief has coexisted with growth in the resources available for development.The breadth of the expansion matters as much as its scale. Reported taxable supplies grew across all 11 sector groups and all major states. Growth across sectors and regions creates opportunities for more businesses to participate in expanding markets, and for more communities to benefit from the demand, investment and employment that follow.Reported sales to consumers (B2C) rose 26.7% in the post-reform comparison. When tax relief is reflected in prices, families have more room to meet other needs or save. Consumer relief and enterprise growth are closely connected: the purchasing power of households sustains demand for the goods and services that businesses provide. The benefits can extend from the household to the retailer, the supplier and the producer.For small and medium enterprises, a national market is valuable when it opens a practical route to customers beyond their immediate surroundings. Businesses in tier-2 and tier-3 towns should be able to build those relationships while continuing to invest and employ people locally. Enterprises expanding into these towns, in turn, can create opportunities for local suppliers and distributors. GST's common framework supports these connections; simpler administration must make them easier to sustain.Participation in that framework is substantial. GST registrations across central and state jurisdictions were about 17.1 million at the end of August, up nearly 15% from a year earlier. For the April-July 2026 tax periods, GSTR-3B returns filed by their due dates were 12.6% higher. These improvements place a corresponding responsibility on the administration: regular compliance must be supported by reliable service, clear guidance and timely resolution of difficulties.The functioning of input tax credit is another important part of this experience. The post-reform figures show that the share of tax liability discharged through credits rose, while accumulated credit declined relative to taxable supplies.This is encouraging for businesses that depend on the effective use of eligible credit. For a smaller firm, working capital determines how readily it can purchase inputs, fulfil an order and take on the next one. Refunds are equally relevant. About ₹1.80 lakh crore was refunded during April-September. Returning amounts due to businesses is part of a well-functioning tax system. Greater predictability in this process would help enterprises plan purchases and production with more confidence.(The writer is the union minister of finance and corporate affairs.)

Brahmastra Builds Ammunition Demilitarisation Capability
morning.text:
Indian defence company Brahmastra Explosives and Ammunition is gearing up to meet the need for the safe and controlled demilitarisation of unserviceable ammunition, both in the domestic and international markets. The company is working towards providing professional and compliant solutions for the destruction of spent munitions, while being committed to the principles of safety and environmental responsibility.
Focus on unserviceable ammunition
Ammunition needs to be managed throughout its lifecycle, including during the phase when it becomes unserviceable or unfit for use. Brahmastra announced its plan to address this growing need by offering its services in the demilitarisation of various types of ammunition, ranging from small-calibre rounds to mortar and artillery projectiles. It added that the proposed solution fits into an ammunition lifecycle-management system, whereby aged or defective stocks are removed from inventory through secure and controlled channels.
Experienced ammunition professionals
The company noted that its demilitarisation expertise would be provided by senior ammunition technical officers with over four decades of experience in the field. It mentioned that the know-how and experience would contribute to developing responsible and effective solutions for the safe handling of ammunition lots. According to Brahmastra, the focus on safety and compliance will be a key enabler in meeting the rising demand for responsible ammunition lifecycle management.
Potential for domestic and global markets
Brahmastra is targeting both the domestic and international markets. The company sees opportunities for providing demilitarisation solutions for domestic needs, as well as for meeting global demand for such services. In addition to supporting India’s national security objectives, the proposed solution addresses the need to manage aged and unserviceable ammunition in a safe and responsible manner.
For other countries, the management of outdated and defective munitions is also a matter of safety, as well as efficient logistics and storage management. For India, the ability to offer such services would create additional growth opportunities for the domestic private defence industry.
India eyes ammunition lifecycle management
Brahmastra announced its plans to help India evolve as a global centre of excellence in responsible and safe lifecycle management of ammunition. This builds on India’s proposed vision for defence manufacturing, which includes not only the production of new defence platforms but also their lifecycle management.

morning.title: Lockheed Martin May Expand Indian Production if It Wins Transport Deal
morning.text:
Lockheed Martin is looking to further expand its production capabilities in India if it wins the bid to supply medium transport aircraft for its armed forces, a senior official of the aerospace company said.
In August, India issued a tender for procurement of 60 medium transport aircraft at a cost of USD 10.5 billion.
Five Indian companies — Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL), Mahindra Group, Adani Defence & Aerospace, Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) and Reliance Defence — are in the fray for the contract and are expected to bring global aircraft manufacturers into the programme.
“We have a long partnership with Tata that produces components and empennages of the C-130J aircraft. It is a very robust capability that will be expanded in our current bid,” Dan Tenney, Senior Vice President, global business development and strategy, Lockheed Martin, said in response to a question from PTI.
“We are looking to expand that capability with production and other things that occur within India,” he said.
TASL has partnered with Lockheed Martin, while Mahindra has joined hands with Brazil’s Embraer for the contract.
“So we’re very excited by that. India has been a great partner in helping to enable advanced capabilities for that aircraft and beyond,” Tenney said.
He said if Lockheed Martin and TASL are successful in that bid, the network will be expanded.
“So we are looking to do that,” Tenney said.
Lockheed Martin said its proposal would include 12 aircraft in flyaway condition and 48 manufactured in India.
The company has also proposed upgrading the Indian Air Force’s (IAF) existing fleet of 12 C-130Js to the same advanced configuration, potentially giving the force a common fleet of 72 aircraft.
The IAF’s current C-130J fleet has accumulated more than 58,000 flight hours and is used for high-altitude operations in Ladakh, humanitarian missions during the Nepal floods and the evacuation of Indian nationals from Sudan in 2023.

morning.title: India Demonstrates 5.56-km Free-Space Quantum Key Distribution Link
morning.text:
QNu Labs, in collaboration with Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo‑informatics (BISAG‑N) and IIT Gandhinagar, has successfully demonstrated India’s first free‑space Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) link at a scale of 5.56 km.
The field trial, conducted on the night of September 27–28, established a secure quantum communication channel between BISAG‑N and IIT Gandhinagar. Using QNu Labs’ Pointing, Acquisition and Tracking system, the trial achieved a stable Quantum Bit Error Rate below 5% and generated secure keys at a rate of 230–260 bps. These keys were integrated with BISAG‑N’s post‑quantum cryptography enabled Vedic Kavach platform, enabling successful end‑to‑end encryption and decryption of test messages.
The demonstration combined two complementary layers of quantum security: QNu Labs’ hardware‑based QKD device Armos over free‑space optical channels and BISAG‑N’s Vedic Kavach software‑based post‑quantum cryptography with quantum random number generation. This integrated architecture ensures resilience even if the physical quantum channel is temporarily unavailable.
Dr. Vinay Thakur, Director General, BISAG‑N, stated that the integration of Vedic Kavach with QNu Labs’ QKD technology marks a significant step towards practical quantum‑resilient communication systems.
Sunil Gupta, Co‑founder and CEO, QNu Labs, emphasized that the successful 5.56 km demonstration paves the way for longer‑distance quantum‑secure networks and satellite‑based quantum communication.
Cmde Manish Tripathi (Retd.), In‑charge, ISTF, IIT Gandhinagar, added that the demonstration provides a valuable field environment for advancing practical quantum communication technologies and showcases how academia, indigenous technology and real‑world experimentation can be integrated to meet emerging secure communication requirements.
The trial provides a foundation for advancing India’s capabilities in secure communication infrastructure, strengthening resilience against emerging quantum‑era security threats.
About BISAG‑N: An autonomous scientific society under MeitY, BISAG‑N works in space technology applications, satellite communication, geo‑informatics and supports technology‑driven governance.
About IIT Gandhinagar: Founded in 2008, the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar (IITGN) is a leading institution focused on excellence in engineering, science, technology, humanities and social sciences. The Institute promotes interdisciplinary research, innovative education and solutions to real-world challenges.
About QNu Labs: Founded in 2016, QNu Labs is India’s pioneer in quantum‑secure digital infrastructure, offering sovereign products and solutions deployed globally.

morning.title: Lions and cheetahs and chimps, oh my: a spotlight on Africa's diverse wildlife
morning.text:
Chimps fish for algae in a rare example of primate tool use. Credit: National Geographic

A wild African black panther prowls for prey. An orphaned baby pangolin must learn how to climb on its own. And a green turtle struggles to make it back to the water after laying her eggs on a remote island, rescued by local humans who carry the exhuasted turtle to the water's edge. These animals and many other species are featured in Africa: Earth's Wild Home, a new documentary series from National Geographic. It's meant to launch a new franchise, with separate series documenting the wildlife and environmental ecosystems of all seven continents in turn.

The seven-episode documentary series took four years to complete, with filming taking place across nearly 30 different African countries. Each episode focuses on a specific ecosystem, from the jungle and the desert, to the plains, mountains, and islands of Africa, and closes by spotlighting the various scientists, photographers, and NatGeo explorers whose work made the series possible. The final episode focuses on the local conservation leaders and researchers working to preserve Africa's rich biodiversity for future generations.

The producers found the perfect narrator in Wunmi Mosaku, who has delivered powerful performances in such works as Sinners, Loki, and Lovecraft Country. "I was incredibly honored that they even know my name at Nat Geo," Mosaku told Ars. "It was wonderful to be asked to narrate the series, it means so much to me. As someone who was born in Nigeria and raised in England, I'll take any opportunity I can to reconnect and celebrate this incredible continent where life is so diverse and so extreme and beautiful and relentless and peaceful. I wanted to be a part of that because it's a part of me."
